body:
Personally, I don't think adding a global `get_seed()` function is a good idea.

If we do add a global function, it should have a much less generic name to avoid causing confusion with user-defined functions. At the very least `get_random_seed()` - more specific would be even better, but I can't think of any other good options :-)

That said, I think [the](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615#issuecomment-1284497804) [suggestions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615#issuecomment-1452523811) on the original proposal are a much better idea than adding a global function.

In particular, I quite like the suggestion of adding `RandomNumberGenerator.shuffle(array)` to cover that case. A similar approach could be used for any other cases in the API where the global random number generator is used

> Personally, I don't think adding a global `get_seed()` function is a good idea.
> 
> If we do add a global function, it should have a much less generic name to avoid causing confusion with user-defined functions. At the very least `get_random_seed()` - more specific would be even better, but I can't think of any other good options :-)
> 
> That said, I think [the](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615#issuecomment-1284497804) [suggestions](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615#issuecomment-1452523811) on the original proposal are a much better idea than adding a global function.
> 
> In particular, I quite like the suggestion of adding `RandomNumberGenerator.shuffle(array)` to cover that case. A similar approach could be used for any other cases in the API where the global random number generator is used

Why do you think it's not a good idea? I do understand the naming change--I didn't think about user-defined functions. The best name I can think of is `get_global_random_seed()` or maybe just `get_global_seed()`. 

I'm not sure about Godot's design philosophy. Is it give users everything neatly organized? If so, I think there's no reason _not_ to add this function with a better name. However, if the goal is to make the engine as consistent as possible with a lower likelihood of possible bugs or things breaking, maybe it's a good idea not to.

Personally, I'm on the side of keeping the function, but I do think that `RandomNumberGenerator.shuffle(array)` would be nice to have as well. It really just comes down to if we want easy access to something slightly more risky.

Finally, maybe there's some way we could put it in the documentation/hover info that it's not recommended to use it this way, or maybe just suggest a better method? I'm not sure on that front.

I feel like the replies in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615 nicely summarize my feelings on this. But I have a few extra remarks:

- If this PR is approved, there would be little reason [not to expose `rand_weighted` to the global scope](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104412#pullrequestreview-2760795551), as well.
	- There's not much consensus or interest on this.
	- And at that point, the entire global **RandomNumberGenerator** object may as well be exposed, which itself is a very questionable choice.
- [As mentioned in the proposal](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/5615#issuecomment-1284497804), exposing `get_seed` would further encourage using the global methods for reproducible RNG sequences.
	- There's plenty of reasons to discourage this, but I don't believe there's anything explicitly documenting it.
	- I say "further" because, one may argue exposing `seed` (`set_seed`) itself was a bit of a mistake.
		- _I don't necessarily agree with this. `seed` is a good method for prototyping and testing purposes. Just food for thought_.

The reasons not to expose the functions makes a lot of sense. However:
 
> * _`seed` is a good method for prototyping and testing purposes. Just food for thought_.

I didn't know this until I looked and searched the web. I think, if we don't implement the get_seed() function, it would be helpful if somewhere it mentions that it's not intended for "production use."

> Why do you think it's not a good idea?

I think we should avoid adding new global functions as much as possible. It's more things to collide with user-defined variables or methods, leading to annoying `SHADOWED_GLOBAL_IDENTIFIER` warnings, confusion, or accidentally selecting the wrong method.

Some global functions are well-known and used in a several other languages too (like `ord()` or `abs()`) and those are less bad, because I think folks already sort of expect them. Whereas something like `get_seed()` is more similar to a function name a user might define, making a collision more likely

> it would be helpful if somewhere it mentions that it's not intended for "production use."

Oh, I mean, you can absolutely use it in production! Let's be clear here because it's not dangerous or anything. It's just that if RNG becomes a very important component of your project, it's more reasonable to use your own RandomNumberGenerator instance, instead.

I would suggest "just" adding a note but that's not enough, I think. I've noticed that the global scope's class reference doesn't make it clear that all of the random methods and **RandomNumberGenerator** are intrinsically related.
